8th April, 1935.

re Max Julius HODANN and LINDBAEK-NILSSON.

The following gives further result of observation on the above-named:

Tuesday, 2nd April:

HODANN at 11.20 a.m. left parcel at Laundry, 44a Gloucester Road. At 1.30 he, with NILSSON and child went to Post Office, 15, Gloucester Road; former despatched one or more registered letters, then to restaurant nearby, afterwards returning to 6, Cornwall Gardens. At 4.30 p.m. NILSSON posted several letters. At 6.15 travelled to Telford Road and then visited the North Paddington Women's Welfare Centre where he remained until 9.10 p.m. and then returned to his lodgings.

Shortly after he arrived at the Welfare Centre, car GK-1523 arrived and lady driver entered. She was still at the Centre when HODANN left.

Wednesday, 3rd April:

HODANN and NILSSON visited J. Lane - Bodley Head Publishing Co., 8, Vigo Street from 11.10 to 11.25 a.m., then Norway House, Cockspur Street 11.35 to 12.25 and after taking lunch at a public house entered Chatham House, St. James' Square from 2.5 to 2.50 p.m. then Transport House, Smith Square, W.1. from 3.25 to 4.40 and afterwards to Chatham House, St. James' Square, from 5 to 6.30 returning home at 7.5 p.m.

Thursday, 4th April:

HODANN left home at 12 noon and called at 8, Blenheim Road, N.W.8. (supposed basement flat) but apparently the person whom he wished to see there was not at home, as he came from the house after a few minutes and waited outside 45 minutes, then made a phone call and returned to the house for a minute or so, after which he went to Flat 37, Hartington Court, Lansdowne Road, from 2.30 to 4.15 then to Chatham
